original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Changed hypothesis: free per-register address twists B -> P B Q (P, Q in GL_m(Z_(2))) between paid calls, which the three-register bound and its successors exclude; with binary mixing and any number of restored dirty roles. Question: can such twists beat sum_s rank(C_s mod 2) (nine for three targets invertible mod 2)? Domain: odd-denominator frames, formal group-algebra identities.
scope_change_reason: The card allows a specified nonabelian operation family. Twisted XORs make the operator ring a skew group ring F2[H] x| G with an abelian address group, unlike the nonabelian address groups (Q8, D16, GL_n(F2), A5, ...) already studied. Free address maps are the hypothesis every predecessor names as excluded.
bottleneck_link: Side result for the bit primitive: it decides whether free relabellings can reduce the paid call count of the bit interchange. One-sided relabellings cannot in the odd-denominator domain. For two-sided relabellings, the square-zero obstruction is shown to be powerless, which isolates what an exact saving or a stronger cut must handle.
stop_rule: Stop after a uniform proof for one explicit twist model plus an exact finite witness or obstruction for the complementary model. Do not run open-ended searches over the S3 x S3 twist alphabet in this session.
evidence: Written proof of Theorem A (PROOF.md section 3). Exact skew-ring verifier: the direct nine-call word; 240 seeded random one-sided-twist words satisfying the flattening bound, with the opposite flattening exceeding it; and all 5040 orders of the seven-call two-sided witness agreeing with the target in the square-zero image, none exact. Mutation controls are rejected.

open_questions.question: Can two-sided address twists (for example B -> S B S^T) realize three invertible targets with fewer than nine paid calls exactly?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A yes would change the paid count of the bit primitive under a free-relabelling premise. A no would extend the floor to all PBQ twists.
open_questions.first_step: Compute the order-two term (modulo the cube of the augmentation ideal) of the seven-call frame multiset over all S3 x S3 twist assignments, to obtain a second-order cut or a candidate.
open_questions.blocked_by: Size of the twist alphabet, and the lack of a rank invariant robust to F2[G] zero divisors.

open_questions.question: Does the native bit supplier implement a per-register PBQ address relabelling without paid work?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A formal saving matters only if the relabelling is legal and cheaper than the call it saves.
open_questions.first_step: Identify which address maps the selected bit word's physical layout applies for free.
open_questions.blocked_by: No native model of address relabelling in this package.

open_questions.question: Do words mixing left-only and right-only twists evade the floor?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Neither flattening applies directly, so this is the smallest gap between Theorem A and the open two-sided case.
open_questions.first_step: Run an exact square-zero relaxation search with left and right axis swaps and at most eight calls.
